subject: Infra suitability check & follow-up — deployment mode and isolation concerns
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@medcorehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 14:10:00 -0800
Subject: Infra suitability check & follow-up — deployment mode and isolation concerns

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for the time today. Wanted to recap the items we heard and propose concrete next steps so your security and infra teams have what they need. Short version: we heard three core priorities from your team — predictable P99 latency, data isolation/residency, and transparent telemetry for audit. Those map to different deployment options (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) so I outlined our recommended path below.

Summary of what we captured:
- Peak workload: ~120 reqs/sec with bursts up to ~450 reqs/sec during daily batch windows.
- Latency targets: P50 ~20–30ms, P95 <120ms, P99 target 200ms (hard SLO for product).
- Data concerns: PHI-adjacent workflows, must keep logs in US-only, and limited 3rd-party exposure.
- Risk tolerance: low — noisy neighbor risk currently unacceptable to the infra team without clear mitigations.

Recommendation (quick read):
1) Short term: dedicated GPU pool (Redwood Dedicated) with reserved capacity and SLA — minimizes noisy-neighbor risk and gives predictable unit economics.
2) Compliance: we can provide our SOC 2 report and a scoped technical annex for data residency.
3) Long term: consider Private (VPC) if you require full control or air-gapped deployment — we can map timeline and packaging next call.

Attachments: I attached a short 'Redwood deployment options' PDF that maps capabilities + tradeoffs.

Next steps I propose:
- Share your procurement contact and any internal SLO rubric (we noted P99 = 200ms).
- Schedule a 60-min technical deep dive with our infra engineering and your platform team (Ben/Marissa to join).
- We will send SOC2 + a short ops playbook and a PoC checklist for Dedicated capacity.

If that sounds right, can you do a technical deep dive next Tue (Dec 15) at 10am ET / 7am PT?

Best,

Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.com | (415) 555-0127
Redwood Inference

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@medcorehealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@medcorehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Infra suitability check & follow-up — deployment mode and isolation concerns

Thanks, Stephanie — good recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Volume & latency: the burst numbers are accurate; we also have periodic long-context jobs (avg seq length 1,600 tokens) that increase memory/KV-cache pressure.
- SLOs: P99 200ms is non-negotiable for us on the inference path tied to triage flows. If you cannot meet that predictably on shared/hosted, we need options.
- Isolation: noisy neighbor risk is the showstopper for our infra team; we need either a dedicated tenant or clear hard isolation guarantees (CPU/GPU allocation and network segmentation).
- Audit: our security team will request SOC2 plus evidence of per-customer audit logs and key management.

Attaching our short security questionnaire (SSQ) and procurement terms for your review. Also, please call out whether the Dedicated option has a documented SLA for P99 latency, and any examples of customers running similar workloads.

Can you also confirm whether redwood's caching/prefixing strategies would introduce cross-tenant inference artifacts? That is, are cached prefixes or KV caches ever reused across customers? That is one of our security team's explicit asks.

Thanks — Sam

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Infra suitability check & follow-up — deployment mode and isolation concerns

Team — quick internal note before we respond to Sam's SSQ:

- Dedicated looks like the right immediate pathway. It buys isolation and predictable latency. We can commit to a reserved pool sized for their steady state + headroom for bursts.
- Action items for pre-sales:
  * Ben: draft a capacity config and provisional pricing for a 6-12 month reserved commitment (include burst/overage terms).
  * Ops/Eng (I'll loop in privately): prepare a short technical annex that explains how KV cache/prefixing is scoped per-tenant and what guarantees we offer for key separation. Include a paragraph on per-customer KMS integration options.
  * Stephanie: send SOC2/controls pack and propose the technical deep dive time.
- PoC ask: offer a 2-week Dedicated PoC with metrics collection (latency heatmaps, token costs, traced request IDs) so MedCore can validate P99 under realistic load.

Keep replies tight — include a clear ask for the procurement contact and their desired contracts cadence (master services agreement + SOW) so we can align legal.

Marissa
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@medcorehealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@medcorehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 08:00:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed next steps & technical deep dive scheduling

Sam —

Appreciate the rapid clarifications. Based on Marissa's notes above, here's a concrete path forward that addresses the noisy-neighbor and SLO concerns:

1) Dedicated reserved pool PoC (recommended near-term)
   - 2-week PoC on a dedicated Redwood pool sized to your steady state + 2x burst headroom.
   - We will collect P50/P95/P99, request/response traces, and KV-cache pressure metrics.
   - Goal: validate P99 < 200ms under your peak patterns.

2) Security & audit deliverables
   - We will send our SOC2 report and a technical annex detailing per-tenant isolation, KMS options, and audit-log retention (attached).
   - Answering your explicit question: KV caches and prefix caches are scoped per-tenant; they are never reused across customers. We'll include the exact isolation paragraph in the tech annex.

3) Commercial & procurement
   - Ben will follow up with a provisional pricing sheet for a 6/12 month reserved commitment and burst/overage terms.
   - I've attached a draft Mutual Action Plan (MUA) to jumpstart contract discussions.

Proposed meeting: Tue, Dec 15, 2026 at 10:00am ET — 60-min technical deep dive with our infra engineers and your platform & security reps. If that works, share the attendee list and any extra telemetry you'd like captured during the PoC.

Attachments: medcore-soc2-and-security.pdf, mua-draft.docx

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

Best,

Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
